state.misconception_label: Assumes that an arrow on a number line starts at zero

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: I have: ![Number line with -12 and -7 marked. Starting at -12, follow an arrow pointing to the right labelled +10. Then there is an arrow labelled b pointing to the left, which ends at -7 on the number line.]() What is the value of \( b \) ? I got \( -7 \) because I'm not sure I worked it out the right way.

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Let me ask you this: what would happen if you considered the direction of the arrow on the number line in relation to the starting point of -12?

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: Oh, so like... the arrow starts at -12, not at zero? So I need to work out where -12 plus 10 gets me first, and then figure out what b is from there? Is that what you mean?

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Exactly, you're on the right track. How would you calculate where -12 plus 10 gets you on the number line before determining the value of \( b \)?

score.justification_pass1: The teacher effectively addresses the zero-starting misconception by directing attention to the actual starting point (-12), and the student demonstrates clear progress by articulating the correct two-step approach, though the final calculation isn't completed.
score.justification_pass2: The teacher consistently uses probing questions to guide the student's thinking without revealing the answer, helping them recognize their error in starting point and leading them to discover the correct approach independently.
